newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BA's Ayling "disappointed" by strike ballot call.
newsitem.headline: BA's Ayling "disappointed" by strike ballot call.

text.p: British Airways chief executive Robert Ayling said on Monday he was dismayed by strike threats from the airline's ground staff at London's Heathrow and Gatwick airports and pledged to keep aircraft flying regardless.
"I am very disappointed because we have worked very well with the TGWU (Transport and General Work Union) in a number of areas," Ayling told reporters.
The union announced on Monday that it is to hold a strike ballot among 9,000 ground staff members including baggage handlers, clerical and check-in workers and catering staff.
Ayling said staff would not back the strike call, results of which are due out on June 30.
"I am optimistic that the employees in the company will not support strike action.

"We have made extensive contingency plans. We are determined to keep flying," said Ayling, who was in Brussels to discuss BA's planned partnership with AMR Corp's American Airlines with European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert.
Ayling rejected union accusations that plans to sell the long-haul catering business presaged a wider service sell-off to outside contractors.

"We have taken a number of decisions not to out-source activities where we think they could be maintained competitively within the organisation but in the case of catering... we are facing a rapidly changing situation in the world market where competiveness can only be maintained in the much larger airline catering groups," he said.
Ayling added that plans to offload the long-haul catering business, announced in April, would go ahead only if a "reputable buyer" could be found.
